You've tried GPTs; now try Saiqic

I have a stupidly simple strategy to grow any website without paid backlinks or PR. 
There are only three phases involved in it. 

Phase 1: Main core pages. 
This is the easiest part. All I have to do is to get to the DNA of the business, do very basic market research, and strategize the core pages. 

a) 3-4 essential pages = Homepage + About + contact
(the name of these pages vary as per the business)

b) Main service/solution pages. 
Could be 3-6…depending on what the business offers. 

In this phase, the strategy is not hard…but I have to pour my blood & sweat into the copy. 

Phase 2: Sub-service pages. 
That’s where I need high-level market research + KW opportunities,etc. 
Each main service page acts as a pillar here. 
And based on the business dimensions and ICPs, we expand the pages.
Usually I target 4-5 in each pillar. And then if the industry/use cases are applicable then more pages. 

(This is not programmatic SEO. Much different. It’s more like building a semantic architecture of the website)

Phase 3: BOFu blog content + off-page SEO
We’re done with the core + supporting pages. 
Now’s the time to cover those pages from all the remaining angles…so we strategize buying-intent/ICP focused blog content. 
Each service page gets 2-4 topics.

Along with this we start submitting business on relevant directories with proper profiling & stuff and create social media + forum profiles. 

On average, this takes 3-4 months. We create upto 50 pages. 
Usually it starts showing results after 5 months. 

I cant possibly share the whole thing in 250 words posts…so if you would like to hear more, you can book a free discovery call. Bring your site and I will customize every point on the call to your business. 
#mrsaiqo

Call it my dumbest mistake or innocence, but this once cost me & team a $2500 monthly contract. 
This was when I started taking full-stack SEO+content projects. 
A client approached. He had just started his insurance agency. We had the meeting. He wanted us to take care of his website from scratch and everything, including SEO + content + management. 

After the meeting, he asked for the detailed proposal and how we’d approach & execute the whole thing, along with the pricing. 
Took me around 3-4 hours, and I sent a proposal that stated everything we’ll do in the next 3 months.
He liked it & asked me to devise the proposal for 12 months & how I would expand my strategies & how much total it’d cost him and expected results. 
I spent another 4-5 hours and drafted the whole proposal. 
Now the proposal was like a blueprint of how to scale the website. 
Even the structure of some pages & the organization of the site. 
Custom strategies that I built specifically for his website. 

He received the proposal. Thanked us. 
And then ghosted:)

My gut signaled that he’d have uploaded the whole strategy to Claude. 
And then after some time I stalked his site and saw a very poor & pathetic version of my strategies implemented with very low quality content:)

Was I dumb or innocent to hand over the whole strategy before signing a contract? Idk. But it taught me a thing or two.

#mrsaiqo

Hey, this is my post to myself. You can scroll past…I’m just trying to get back:)

I posted 30+ times in the past 7 months…
But I wasnt feeling connected or invested in here. 

3 months ago, I almost had no clients. When you’re in a service business, clients come & go. That’s nothing unusual. You have to have a thick skin. I’m still developing one.  

So many things have been happening since the start of 2026.

Changes in our SEO+ content industry, AI, my agency Saiqic, identity crisis, imposter syndrome, uncertainty… & a lot of other stuff. In some areas I’m floating, in some I’m struggling, and some I’ve conquered. 

I’ve learned & sought so much that now I’ll have to sit with myself, let everything absorb & then find words to share here:) 

How far I’ve come…
How far I still have to go.
All I have to do is stick with what I do best. 

If you know/remeber me, drop a comment to say hi & if you’ve got any questions related to SEO + content, I’d love to answer.

#mrsaiqo

She's been my inspiration for so many things I have done till then. 
Her work ethic and down-to-earth nature, love for the craft- I tried to mimic everything a beginner could from a senior.
 
When I think about design, I think about Sadaf...and whenever I hire a designer for something, I show them her designs:)

This is a bit of a struggling phase for her & I know she'll eventually come out of it. Stronger. More resilient. 
If you need a LinkedIn revamp or someone to manage your LinkedIn account, she's the one. 
If you don't need LinkedIn help, please repost her post and spread the word. 

May Allah bless you.
